body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_plumbing_emergency_google_status_quo
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Apex Plumbing in Denver. They are direct, busy, and skeptical because most urgent plumbing leads already come through Google calls. They should challenge why a plumber needs a website when people search, call the Google listing, and want fast help. They should ask whether the agent is promising more emergency jobs and should push back if the agent sounds like a generic restaurant or menu pitch. If the agent earns enough trust, the user may agree to receive the free mockup link or ask for a short callback.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent states the reason early, adapts to a plumbing business, acknowledges Google calls may already work, and gives one concrete non-guaranteed value angle such as service-area clarity, emergency/non-emergency service separation, trust before a call, license/insurance visibility only if the buyer raises trust, or one page the owner controls. It should not promise more jobs, faster dispatch, higher rankings, or emergency-call lift. If the buyer asks about the catch, it should answer directly that the mockup is free to review with no obligation. If the buyer gives an email, it must confirm the send/reply path and give a natural closing. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, attacks Google, repeats the same website-value point across objections, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, keeps pitching after a clear no, or claims results that are not in the dynamic variables.

body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_dental_compliance_new_patient_claims
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the office manager at Bright Lane Dental in Raleigh. They are careful about medical-adjacent claims and do not want a caller implying guaranteed new patients, treatment outcomes, or anything that sounds noncompliant. They should ask what the mockup would actually show and whether the agent is trying to sell a marketing package. They should become open only if the agent keeps the offer factual, avoids health claims, and frames the page as a clearer way to understand services and contact the office.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent adapts to a dental office, avoids medical or patient-acquisition guarantees, and explains the mockup as a simple homepage direction for services, contact path, accepted-insurance or appointment-request clarity only when raised by the buyer, and trust before calling. It should answer directly if asked whether this becomes a paid website conversation later: yes, only if the mockup looks useful and they want to talk next steps. It should keep the first call low-pressure, stop after a clear refusal, and use a natural closing after a completed send path, callback, or stop. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, promises more patients, mentions treatment results, invents compliance expertise, overexplains paid scope without being asked, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, or fails to confirm the send/reply path after an email is provided.

body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_auto_repair_trust_price_skeptic
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Northside Auto Repair in Columbus. They are skeptical of hidden costs and think a website call usually turns into a big project. They should ask what the catch is, whether the mockup is actually free, what a paid website would roughly cost, and whether the site would make people trust the shop more. They should not accept vague promises. If the agent is transparent on price and uses trust framing without guarantees, the user may agree to receive the mockup link.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent adapts to an auto repair shop, answers catch and price concerns in the first direct answer, uses only the approved price anchors when asked, and frames value as trust and clarity rather than guaranteed car count or revenue. Good value angles include showing services clearly, giving one controlled page for estimates and directions, helping first-time customers judge whether the shop fits their issue, and reducing confusion before calls only as a possibility. It must confirm the email send/reply path after the user provides contact details and use a natural closing after that path is complete. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, invents reviews or certifications, promises more jobs, dodges price after a direct ask, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, or repeats the same no-obligation reassurance without progressing.

body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_hvac_busy_dispatch_callback
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the dispatcher or office manager at Summit HVAC in Phoenix during a busy service day. They are not hostile but they want the caller off the phone quickly. They may say technicians are out, phones are busy, and this can wait. If the agent gives a long website pitch, the user should cut it off. If the agent handles time pressure well, the user will offer a callback window such as after 4 or tomorrow morning.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent adapts to an HVAC service business, respects the busy-dispatch context immediately, gives only a short reason for the call if needed, captures the callback window, confirms it as a statement, closes naturally, and stops. It should not try to sell through the dispatcher once a callback window is known. It can mention service-area clarity or seasonal service pages only if the buyer asks what the call is about. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, asks unnecessary discovery questions after the callback window is known, restarts the pitch, ignores the time pressure, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, or omits a natural closing on the final callback confirmation.

body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_hair_salon_social_media_objection
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Luna Hair Studio in Tampa. They believe Instagram already does everything because clients look at photos and send DMs for appointments. They should challenge whether a website would duplicate Instagram and should dislike generic phrases like online presence or clear path. They may soften if the agent gives a sharper, salon-specific reason without attacking Instagram. If they ask how to see it, they should provide an email and expect the send path to be confirmed.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent adapts to a hair salon, explicitly says Instagram may already be useful, and frames the mockup as a proof test for one owner-controlled link, service categories, stylist/gallery organization, policy or hours clarity, or a cleaner place to send new clients before they DM. It should use plain spoken language and avoid abstract phrases when challenged. It must not push booking software unless the buyer asks. It should confirm the send/reply path after email capture and give a natural closing. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, attacks Instagram, repeats the same organized-information point, pushes online booking after the buyer rejects it, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, or fails to confirm the send/reply path after email capture.

body.name: ELEVENLABS-014-cross-vertical-local-business-simulation-tests::sim_cross_vertical_home_cleaning_gatekeeper_stop_boundary
body.simulation_scenario: The simulated user answers the phone for FreshNest Cleaning in Charlotte but is not the owner. They are polite and can pass a note, but they are not comfortable discussing marketing or pricing. They should ask what the caller wants them to tell the owner. If the agent gives a long pitch or asks the staff member to evaluate the offer, the user should get uncomfortable. If the agent gives a short note and asks for the best callback time, the user may say the owner is usually available after 2.
body.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent adapts to a home-cleaning service, quickly recognizes the gatekeeper role, avoids asking the staff member to judge the offer, gives a short pass-along note only if asked, captures the owner callback window, confirms it as a statement, closes naturally, and stops. The pass-along note should be simple: Emma from Atlas Web Studio, free homepage mockup for FreshNest Cleaning, call after 2. It fails if the agent uses restaurant leakage such as menu, reservations, tables, ordering, restaurant wording, or Mike-related language, continues a full sales pitch to the staff member, asks for private personal contact details, asks the gatekeeper what the agent should tell the owner, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, or omits the closing after the callback or note is complete.
